name: DT Midstream, Inc.
sector: Energy — Natural Gas Midstream (filed under Utilities model fit)
moat_justification: Corridor-monopoly pipelines with ~95% demand-based contracts at ~8-year tenor and a contracted $3.4B backlog, but measured ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) ran only 4.4-5.8% over 2021-2025 — regulated/contracted returns near the cost of capital, not wide-moat pricing power. Gathering carries producer-volume and basin-concentration exposure (Haynesville/Appalachia).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 7.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: High-quality contracted gas midstream, moat 5/10 with regulated-like ~5% ROIC — at $123.67 it clears no hurdle in any scenario (weighted IRR 7.05%, IV@15% $43.34 vs $123.67 price); it would need ~$43 to clear 15%.
moat_for: Natural corridor monopolies: rights-of-way, FERC certificates, replacement cost block competing lines
Premier Haynesville footprint with LEAP delivering into the Gulf Coast LNG corridor; record 2.2 Bcf/d gathering volumes Q2 2026
Contracted growth: $3.4B backlog 2026-2030, ~60% commercialized, >80% pipeline projects, each backed by long-term agreements
Investment-grade balance sheet; rating agencies raised leverage downgrade thresholds in 2026
moat_against: ROIC proxy only 4.4-5.8% (2021-2025) — returns capped by FERC rate proceedings and contract resets
Gathering exposed to producer drilling decisions; Haynesville + Appalachia basin concentration, few large customers
Smaller scale than Kinder Morgan / Williams — less diversification
Key pipelines partly held as JV interests (Millennium, NEXUS, Vector), not wholly controlled
Long-tail natural gas demand / energy-transition risk
